readmeTitle: Collab Deal OS — Full case study

readmeSections.heading: Creator–Brand Collaboration Marketplace & Deal Management Platform
readmeSections.text: Collab Deal OS is a full-stack collaboration platform designed to bring brands and creators into one structured marketplace. Instead of handling collaborations through scattered DMs, emails, spreadsheets, and social-media comments, the platform provides a dedicated environment where brands can publish opportunities, creators can discover and express interest in deals, and both sides can move from discovery to private conversation and offers.

readmeSections.heading: How the project evolved
readmeSections.text: The project started as an experiment around managing collaboration deals, but evolved into a broader creator–brand marketplace and communication system with role-based workspaces, realtime messaging, deal discovery, creator discovery, offers, and creator-to-creator networking.

readmeSections.heading: Core marketplace flow
readmeSections.text: Brand publishes a deal → Creator discovers it → Creator comments or shows interest → Brand reviews interested creators → Private conversation begins → Collaboration terms can be discussed through the platform. Accounts operate strictly as either a Creator or Brand, giving each role its own navigation, permissions, dashboard, and workflow.

readmeSections.heading: Creator-to-Creator Connect
readmeSections.text: Creators can network through marketplace discussions. A creator can start a private conversation with another creator directly from that creator's comment on a published deal. The system blocks self-messaging and reuses an existing conversation when the same pair reconnects through the same deal, preventing duplicate chats. These conversations remain private to the participating creators.

readmeSections.heading: Realtime messaging system
readmeSections.text: Collab Deal OS supports Brand ↔ Creator and Creator ↔ Creator conversations with realtime delivery through Supabase Realtime, plus client-side synchronization designed to keep conversations responsive and reliable.

readmeSections.heading: Brand workspace
readmeSections.text: Brands receive a dedicated workspace for running collaboration campaigns without exposing brand-management functionality to creator accounts.

readmeSections.heading: Creator workspace
readmeSections.text: Creators receive a separate experience for maintaining their profile, discovering opportunities, commenting to show interest, communicating privately with brands, connecting with creators through deal discussions, and managing offers.

readmeSections.heading: Authentication and authorization
readmeSections.text: The platform supports Google OAuth through Supabase Auth. Authorization is enforced at the database level: Supabase Row Level Security policies restrict conversations and protected information according to the authenticated user's role and participation. Creator-to-creator conversations, for example, are accessible only to their two participants.

readmeSections.heading: Database and backend architecture
readmeSections.text: Supabase and PostgreSQL store creator and brand profiles, campaigns and deals, comments, conversations, messages, offers, authentication relationships, and access-control rules. PostgreSQL functions and RPCs handle sensitive operations such as starting conversations. For creator networking, the backend verifies that the target creator participated in the selected published deal instead of trusting an arbitrary client request.

readmeSections.heading: UI and UX
readmeSections.text: The interface uses a soft neo-brutalist design system with strong borders, hard shadows, compact rounded corners, bold typography, and responsive layouts. Desktop hover-dependent actions were adapted for touch devices, messaging received dedicated mobile work, and the floating Quick Actions button uses a premium animated glowing-border treatment.

readmeSections.heading: Technology stack
items: Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
Authentication: Supabase Auth and Google OAuth

readmeSections.heading: Engineering challenges
readmeSections.text: A major challenge was making messaging behave like a realtime communication product rather than a database-backed inbox. Earlier versions could require a refresh before received messages appeared, so the architecture was improved with realtime subscriptions and additional synchronization while preserving replies and message deletion. Creator ↔ Creator messaging also had to be added without breaking the existing Brand ↔ Creator model, requiring explicit conversation types and participant relationships while maintaining compatibility.

readmeSections.heading: Mobile messaging challenges
readmeSections.text: Long messages, URLs, menus, reply actions, and message controls could overflow or become inaccessible on smaller screens. The layouts and interactions were adjusted so important actions remain available on touch devices without depending on desktop hover states.

readmeSections.heading: Security and data isolation
readmeSections.text: The application treats database access controls—not frontend visibility—as the security boundary. Policies distinguish Brand–Creator from Creator–Creator conversations, block non-participants from private creator conversations through the normal authenticated client, and use controlled database functions with validation for sensitive conversation creation.

readmeSections.heading: Impact and status
readmeSections.text: Status: Active / Live. Current release: v1.2.0. Platform: Web application. Deployment: Cloudflare Workers. Database: Supabase/PostgreSQL. Development: AI-assisted full-stack development.

readmeSections.heading: Project impact
readmeSections.text: Collab Deal OS became one of my larger full-stack projects because it moved beyond a static interface into a functioning multi-role application involving authentication, relational data, realtime communication, database authorization, marketplace interactions, responsive design, production migrations, testing, and cloud deployment. It represents my progression from frontend work toward understanding how a production-style application connects UI → authentication → backend logic → PostgreSQL → realtime systems → authorization → testing → deployment.
